## Research cost model + two structural rules for this design

Cluster 7 numbers, and two rules that shape the operations design:

- **Cost model.** Corpus ≈ 107,639 chunks ≈ **27–54M tokens**. A full re-embed costs **$0.27–$0.54** (text-embedding-3-small batch, $0.01/1M) up to **~$3.50–$7.00** (3-large standard, $0.13/1M); self-hosted BGE-M3 ≈ $0.001/1M at high utilization. So the corpus is cheap — **churn is the driver**: re-embedding the unchanged 95% on every log version, forever, plus 5–20× growth from the comments/docs expansion. Against the plan cap (Turso scaler $24.92/mo), embedding spend is a rounding error *if* deltas work; **storage and DB-count quotas bind first**. The ledger metric that proves deltas work is the **delta reuse ratio** — per batch `(chunks_new, chunks_reused, tokens, model, $)`; **reuse <90% on an append-mostly source means the delta protocol is broken, not the budget** (ledger design: [#6058](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6058)).
- **The secret tier is embedded LOCALLY, regardless of price.** Sending secret-tier text to a hosted embedding API is a classification violation at any cost; the local route's marginal cost is electricity, which also caps plan-spend risk structurally. That raises a comparability question the design must answer (different models per tier → different vector spaces → fan-out merge assumptions): [#6060](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6060).
- **Ingest publishes through a staging gate, never directly to the live corpus** — write → classify → dedup → provenance-check → publish (lakeFS write-audit-publish pattern; staging tier [#5669](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5669) exists). A failed batch never touches the searchable corpus. Gate design: [#6057](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6057).
- Delta discovery is **metadata-first**: a per-source manifest `(path, size, mtime, head-hash)` decides skips without opening files (the 21 GB rule: discovering the delta must not read the 21 GB), with sampled full-verification passes so mtime lies get caught. That protocol lives in the delta design ([#6028](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6028) / research item 37, mapped there).

### Wave-2 children filed under this issue

- [#6045](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6045) — in-toto-shaped per-batch statement (subjects/materials/builder)
- [#6057](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6057) — classify → dedup → provenance-check → publish
- [#6058](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6058) — per-batch accounting + reuse-ratio alert
- [#6059](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6059) — model selection; no-egress invariant
- [#6060](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6060) — normalization contract or one-model mandate
- [#6061](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6061) — churn × retention simulation calibrating retention defaults


— Wave-2 research fold-in, 2026-11-04 (prior-art doc: `~/workspace/scratch/atlas-ingestion-brief-2026-11-04/prior-art-research.md`)
